text:
dmitri: quick thought — can we add an "advisory" header set for saturated pools instead of only hard 429s?

sarah: +1 can you sketch what that looks like?

dmitri: idea: when a GPU pool is nearing capacity we emit a 200 with normal body but include headers that indicate admission pressure, e.g.:
```
x-rw-queue-estimate-ms: 120
x-rw-accept-prob: 0.35
x-rw-advisory-expire: 15
```
- `x-rw-queue-estimate-ms`: best-effort median queue wait
- `x-rw-accept-prob`: probability that a new request will be admitted if retried immediately
- `x-rw-advisory-expire`: TTL (s) for the advisory

The SDK would treat these as signals to apply client-side pacing/backoff, not as errors. That keeps p99 low while avoiding mass retries that make things worse.

jamie: interesting — so we don't block app-level success paths (200) but we give hints for pacing. How does this interact with existing 429s and `Retry-After`?

dmitri: two modes:
- soft-advisory (headers above) when pool is under high but not critical load. No 429s emitted.
- hard-reject (429 + Retry-After) when we need immediate shedding.
SDK logic:
```
if header.x-rw-accept-prob < 0.5:
  delay = draw_from_exp(jitter_base = header.x-rw-queue-estimate-ms)
  schedule_retry(delay)
else:
  proceed
```
We should also emit telemetry: `client_advisory_received` with fields {region, pool, accept_prob, queue_ms}.

sarah: telemetry plz — we need to track false positives where apps overreact and throttle too hard. Also region nuance: some EU pools have long startup tails so queue_estimate is noisy.

dmitri: agreed. plan: pilot on a couple of low-risk endpoints and a single region (us-west2) for 2 weeks, collect:
- % requests seeing advisory headers
- client-side throttle delta (tokens/sec reduced)
- p50/p95/p99 latency changes
- admission fallback rate (how often advisory leads to client retry and eventual admission)

lee: ops-bot note: might be worth adding `x-rw-admit-variant` header so SDKs can prefer cheaper/quantized model variants when accept_prob low. e.g. `admit-variant: small-qa`. This helps cost and latency.

jamie: SDK implications: publish semver-major feature where SDK defaults to passive honoring (log + telemetry) and opt-in active pacing. Docs + migration guide required.

ops-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag `advisory-headers` -> canary on us-west2 -> rollout window 2w.

sarah: +1 on canary. also add a flag to disable advisory-driven retries per-key (customers should be able to opt out).

dmitri: I'll draft a short spec and a telemetry dashboard mock. cc @jamie for SDK changes.

jamie: ack. I'll write the client heuristics PR and include sample metrics to surface in Console.

sarah: thanks — this could smooth the knee in our cost vs latency curve if done right. :rocket:
